en: The Hymn in Fifteen Noble Verses (Āryāpañcadaśīstotra)

I bow to the auspicious one who holds a bow and arrows in her hands, whose feet are like white water-lilies, who generates the pride of the god of love, who removes all impurities, and who bestows the fruits of desired objects. || 1 ||
O Mistress, this voice is not at all capable of praising your greatness;
even Śeṣa, O Great Goddess, has left his own narration of your deeds unfinished after thousands of years.

I bow to Śarvāṇī, who is worthy of supreme worship due to her lordship and other attributes; who shines with a mass of hair as dark as a swarm of bees; whose eyes are like the petals of a blue lotus; and who bestows all that is desired.
I bow to Lalitā, the Mother who is a treasury of the splendor of ten million rising suns, whose feet are sought by the Lord of the Gods;
O young girl, she is the swan in the lotus-heart of the graceful Śiva.
O Daughter of the Snowy Mountain, whose form is the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*, who are worshipped by Viṣṇu, Indra, and Śiva;
O Great Queen, under the white umbrella as bright as the moon, be ever for our welfare! 5.
O faultless one, this moonlight of your smile produces an excess of joy;
it dispels even the poison of Śiva’s throat and the darkness of delusion from the three worlds.
O skillful one, although your feet are capable of granting every desire, why is it that even when you are bowed to,
the celestial wish-fulfilling tree (surataru) is still served by those who possess the power of command, as if it were a granter of fruits only through great hardship?

O you of golden luster, with graceful gait, whose slender waist is bent by the weight of firm breasts, O beloved one with bracelets on your hands and a neck like a conch—homage be to you, O compassionate one! 8.

O you who bring joy to the three-eyed Lord Śiva, who reside upon his lap, who are worshipped by Viṣṇu and the other gods, who serve as the witness to Śiva’s dance, and whose body is half of Śiva’s—salutations to you, O Compassionate One! 9.
O Mother, you whose compassion bestows fortune is capable of making even the Lord of Fortune appear insignificant;
O you who are like a series of waves of the nectar of beauty, please make me the object of that [compassion]. 10.
O Mother Heramba, who are the beloved of Heramba; O Earth, whose womb is the jewel-syllable *hrīṃ*, who shine with breasts like the Hemādri and Mandara mountains—grant me forgiveness eternally! (11)

O Sāvitrī, known through the tradition of the virtuous and consisting of the essential truth of all the Āgamas and Nigamas, place into my mouth this stream of nectar-like eloquent speech, which is the refuge of all aesthetic flavors.
O Kāmākṣī, ocean of compassion, may the bee of my heart drink the nectar of your lotus feet, which are made to blossom by the rays of the sun-stones set in your golden bracelets. 13.
What wonder is there that, by his fearless valor— marked by arms like creepers bearing bows of sugarcane and flowers—
he somehow reduced the multitude of more than a hundred thousand demons to the state of a cloth dyed with turmeric?

O supreme swan, who brings about the awakening of the bliss of my heart, dwell within the lotus of my heart upon the beautiful couch marked by the crescent moon of the one who wears the moon on his crest, in the pleasure-palace of the syllable *hrīṃ*. 15.
For that person of pure intellect who constantly honors that noble Āryāpañcadaśī, the two wives, Lakṣmī and Vāṇī, shall attend upon him with respect. (16)
Thus ends the Āryāpañcadaśīstotra, composed by Tyāgarāja, born of the Kāśyapa lineage and a native of Andhra, who lived as a devotee at the lotus feet of Ānandanātha.
